record: Scientific American Supplement Vol. 57 No. 1483, June 4, 1904, page 23760
facts: The publisher identifies this original issue and credits Nikola Tesla’s article. Its Wardenclyffe photograph is Fig. 2 in the exact issue.

record: Wardenclyffe Laboratory, National Register of Historic Places 100002744, section 7 p. 12 and section 8 p. 28
facts: The footprint retained at the site was the octagonal concrete and stone base. The tower was completed as a timber skeleton and never received its planned copper cladding. It was demolished in 1917.

record: Tesla Science Center official historical account
facts: The transmission tower was built at Wardenclyffe in the early 1900s and designed to support Tesla’s planned communications system.
